findings.title: Device tier is computed once and never re-evaluated on resize/orientation change
findings.where: §3 Device tiering (useDeviceTier reads window.innerWidth once); §5 Tier 2 (width<=768)
findings.problem: useDeviceTier reads window.innerWidth at mount; narrowing a desktop window below 768px or rotating a tablet keeps the initial tier. Not a correctness blocker since the hero is decorative and tier deltas are subtle, but the intended behavior is unstated.
findings.fix: State explicitly that tiering is computed once at mount with no resize listener (acceptable for a decorative hero), OR add a debounced resize listener that recomputes computeTier(...). Pick one and note it in §3.

findings.title: Backdrop grid example markup double-specifies the background size
findings.where: §1 Backdrop grid composition example: bg-grid-fine [background-size:40px_40px] animate-grid-drift
findings.problem: theme.extend.backgroundSize['grid-fine'] already defines 40px 40px and is exposed as a size utility; the arbitrary [background-size:40px_40px] in the example duplicates it. Harmless (same value) but muddies the 'key grid-fine is both image and size' explanation.
findings.fix: Rely on the generated size utility OR keep only the arbitrary [background-size:...], not both. Drop the arbitrary value and let the backgroundSize theme entry apply, or state in one line which utility sets the size.

findings.title: Navbar live clock / SYS NOMINAL status chip has no defined data source or update rule
findings.where: §2 Navbar (live mono 'clock'/SYS NOMINAL status chip on the right)
findings.problem: Unlike the hero telemetry (now fully specified), the clock's format (UTC vs local, HH:MM:SS, Zulu), update cadence, and reduced-motion behavior are unspecified. A per-second setInterval is a motion concern the reduced-motion section does not mention.
findings.fix: Specify clock format and cadence (e.g. HH:MM:SS local or Z UTC, updated every 1000ms, cleared on unmount) and state that under prefers-reduced-motion it freezes or renders a static SYS NOMINAL chip without a ticking time. One sentence in §2.
